(i) we propose a general way of building Lipschitz networks, (ii) we develop a special choice of metric that is beneficial to training, and (iii) we propose a new GAN that out-performs the state of arts in both convergence rate and quality of generated samples, and we provide generalization analysis for this GAN.

1) we propose new building blocks to facilitate constructing deep Lipschitz networks, 2) we propose Dudley GANS, which is a special choice of GANs using the proposed building blocks and Dudley metric, and 3) we provide theoretical analysis of Dudley GANs, which gives rise both to a generalization analysis and to the discovery of a natural link between the proposed Dudley GAN and the empirical risk minimization

(1) it is beneficial to maintain both Lipschitz condition (for stability) and sufficient capacity of a network (for expressiveness) during training; (2) Dudley metric can be used to ensure Lipschiz condition and sufficient capacity, which leads to Dudley GAN; and (3) Dudley GAN can be interpreted as a form of empirical risk minimization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three aspects: (a) theoretical analysis of GAN training and stability (b) practical construction of deep Lipschitz networks (c) empirical evaluation and generalization analysis of GANs.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a new GAN architecture that is stable, efficient, and generalizable.
Dudley GANs are the best GANs in the sense that they converge faster, generate higher quality samples, and have better generalization properties.

we provide both theoretical and practical tools to construct neural networks that have sufficient expressiveness and Lipschitz condition, and use them in the context of GANs to obtain better convergence and sample quality, while providing a natural link between GANs and empirical risk minimizations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel GAN architecture, Dudley GAN, which is more stable and convergent, and also enjoys better sample quality than the state of the art.
we develop both theoretical building blocks and a practical algorithm to construct neural networks with a large range of capacities and expressiveness, and ensure Lipschitz conditions.
we develop a new class of GANs with better convergence and sample quality, which is theoretically well justified.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stability of the training process and the expressiveness of the model are two important aspects of GAN training.
the Lipschitz property is crucial in training generative models and the choice of metric is also important.
one can achieve both stability and expressiveness by using a proper choice of metric and a proper network architecture.
